name: Kandhamal, 2008
summary: After Swami Lakshmanananda Saraswati was shot at his ashram in Tumudibandha, crowds moved through Kandhamal for weeks burning churches and Christian hamlets. Officially 38–39 died; rights groups put the dead near 100 and the displaced in the tens of thousands.
narrative: The killing on 23 August was claimed by Maoists; Sangh organisations blamed Christians and took a funeral procession from Jalespata to Chakapad through the district. A statewide bandh on 25 August opened the worst day. Dalit and Adivasi Christians hid in the forest, then in camps. A nun was raped at K. Nuagaon in front of a police post. Convictions were thin. The Naidu Commission report later went missing from the chief minister’s office.
scaleRationale: One district, weeks of arson. Official deaths in the dozens; displacement of tens of thousands and hundreds of churches destroyed.

resources.note: Kandha–Pana tenure disputes underneath the religious frame

end.note: Killing and arson ran through September; camps lasted longer.

name: Marichjhapi, 1979
summary: The Left Front government blockaded and then cleared Namasudra refugees who had left Dandakaranya camps and settled on Marichjhapi in the Sundarbans. Officially two to eight died. Independent accounts speak of hundreds, or of thousands of families, killed by starvation, disease, firing, and the river.
narrative: Jyoti Basu had promised Sundarbans land while in opposition. In office the island was called a reserve-forest trespass. Police launches ringed it from Republic Day 1979. Tube wells and fisheries were smashed. On 14–16 May the settlement was burnt and the survivors shipped back. No commission sat. Caste, refugee status, and a tiger reserve were the three languages of the same eviction.
scaleRationale: One island, four months. Official deaths are single digits; displacement of thousands of families and an uncensused killing are the reason it is not coded small.

resources.note: Partition refugees refused a Bengal settlement

name: East India communal wave, 1964
summary: After anti-Hindu killings in East Pakistan that followed the Hazratbal relic theft, Calcutta burned in January and the steel towns of Rourkela and Jamshedpur in March, when refugee trains halted on the way to Dandakaranya. Muslims were the main dead in India. Official Indian figures for the two phases sit around 264 and 346; Rourkela’s ethnographic estimates run much higher.
scaleRationale: Three states, two months, hundreds of official deaths and a contested steel-town massacre.

resources.note: East Pakistan Hindu refugees; Indian Muslim flight the other way

name: Ranchi–Hatia, 1967
summary: A week of Hindu–Muslim killing in Ranchi and the Hatia industrial township after an anti-Urdu student march was stoned near Azad High School. The Raghubar Dayal Commission counted 184 dead, 164 of them Muslim.
scaleRationale: Two towns, seven days, under two hundred official dead.

name: Jamshedpur, 1979
summary: A Ram Navami procession through Mango on 11 April turned into two days of killing in Tata’s steel city. Officially 108 dead, 79 of them Muslim. An ambulance of women and children was burnt at Bhalubasa. The Jitendra Narain Commission later blamed the RSS, district officers, and the Bihar Military Police.
scaleRationale: One city, two days, a commission body count of 108.

name: Bhopal, 1992
summary: After the Babri Masjid came down, Bhopal went through two weeks of Hindu–Muslim killing — the deadliest of the 1992 wave in Madhya Pradesh. PUDR counted 139 dead in the city; the Justice K. K. Dubey Commission 143, including fifty civilians in police firing. Twenty-one places in the state were hit; 161 died statewide.
scaleRationale: A state capital plus other MP towns; low hundreds dead and more than a thousand families displaced in Bhopal alone.

name: Rajasthan after Babri, 1992
summary: The day after the Babri demolition, Jaipur’s police fired on crowds near a place of worship. India Today put Rajasthan’s dead at 48; a later academic count of the Jaipur firing is 31 Muslims. Bhilwara and other towns were hit. The Shekhawat government was dismissed. This is not the 2008 Jaipur blasts.
scaleRationale: Statewide but short; official deaths in the low dozens.
